full_judgment:
Syed J R Mudassir Hussain J: This appeal at the instance of defendant No. 4, is directed against the judgment and decree dated 31-5-1990 and 7-5-1990 respectively passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 124 of 1987.

2. The plaintiff-respondent instituted the aforesaid suit against the appellants and others for recovery of possession and his case is that he acquired the suit land by purchase under a registered sale deed dated 24-11-60 and thereafter constructed two storied building thereon and possessed the same and in the month of January, 1971, he left Dhaka for performing Hajj leaving his entire family in the said building and the return of the plaintiff from Hajj was delayed as he was stuck up in West Pakistan.

3. The plaintiff''s further case is that apart from acquiring the suit building he started electric fan making industry in the name and style "Fasons Metal Industries" upon his casehold land bearing plot Nos. 287 and 288 in Baizid Bostami Industrial Area in Chittagong. The plaintiff under much trouble and hardship could procure the Pakistani passport dated 10-2-76 from Sialkot and came to Bangladesh on 29-9-76 and swore an affidavit and surrendered his Pakistani passport owing complete allegiance to Bangladesh but to his utter dismay found that his industry ie Fasons Metal Industry at 287-288, Baizid Bostami Industrial Area was taken over by the Government in his absence and handed over the same to Sena Kalayan Sangstha ie defendant No. 4 and the plaintiff''s scheduled property with two storied building was found under the occupation of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 through defendant No. 1 though the said scheduled property with building was never declared as abandoned property by the Government as informed by letter dated 15-12-1981.

4. The plaintiff, in the meantime was granted citizenship certificate by the Government of Bangladesh on 7-4-78 and he also obtained the citizenship certificate from the Chairman of the Chittagong Pourasabha on 23-8-78 and the property belonged to the plaintiff and he is very much a Bangladesh national. The plaintiff is the owner of the building and the defendant No. 1 being in occupation of the suit property without any lawful authority is liable to be evicted and hence the suit.

5. The defendant Nos. 2,3 and 4 contested the suit by filing separate written statements denied all the material allegations. The defendant Nos. 2 and 3 contended that the suit is not maintainable and plaintiff has no locus standi to file the suit and there is no cause of action. The alleged purchase of the schedule land by the plaintiff from Mr Mahmudun Nabi Chowdhury is not admitted by the defendants. The plaintiff was citizen of Pakistan which was at war and engaged in military operation against the Government of Bangladesh in March, 1971 and he continued to remain as citizen of Pakistan, he left this country for Pakistan with the help of Pakistani Army being a true Pakistani by heart and soul and he having already fled away from Bangladesh ceased to occupy, supervise or manage in person his property acquired as Pakistani on 3-1-72 under the Acting President''s Order of Bangladesh (Taking over the Control and Management of Industrial and Commercial Concern Order, 1972 (Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1972). Thus the Government of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh took over the control and management of the suit property under the provision of the said Acting Presdent''s Order 1 of 1972 in the interest of the Republic and subsequently under Presdent''s Order No. 16 of 1972 and the said property automatically vested in the Government and placed the same under Sena Kallayan Sangstha and the said Sangstha was possessing and managing the property until it was purchased by them under registered sale deed executed by the President of the People''s Republic or Bangladesh on 4-10-80 and the Sena Kallayan Sangstha has been possessing the said peacefully as absolute owner through defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and the plaintiff has got no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land by virtue of his alleged citizenship.

6. The defendant No. 4 the Sena Kallayan Sangstha also filed a written statement taking the similar stand of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 as such, it is not necessary to repeat the same. Upon the aforesaid pleading of the parties the trial Court framed the following issues: "

1. Is the suit maintainable in its present form?

2. Is the suit barred by limitation?

3. Is the enlistment of the suit property as abandoned property by the Government legal.

4. Whether the plaintiff has got interest in the property?

5. Is the plaintiff entitled to get the decree as prayed for.

7. The learned trial Court decreed the suit and hence this appeal.

8. The plaintiff only examined himself as PW 1 and stated that he purchased the suit property from one Mahmudun Nabi Chowdhury by a registered kabala Ext. 1 and his name has been mutated and Khatian has been prepared in his name which is marked as Ext. 3 and he also paid rent vide Ext 4 the rent receipts. He further stated that on 15-12-81 he received a notice from the office of the Executive Engineer, Abandoned House. PWD Division stating that the suit property is not an abandoned property and the said notice is marked as Ext 5. He further stated that he filed Title Suit No. 131/82 for a declaration that the suit property is not an abandoned property and that suit was decreed on 11-1-87 and the said decree is marked as Ext. 6 He further stated that even after getting the said decree the defendants did not vacate the suit premises and for that this suit has been filed for eviction. The plaintiff further stated that it is not a fact he is not a citizen of Bangladesh or that he left Bangladesh or that he left Bangladesh before the war of liberation or his son and family were not here and it is not correct that the defendant did not know about the Title Suit No. 131 of 1982 and he stated that the document dated 4-10-80 in favour of the defendant No. 4 is illegal and plaintiff is not bound by the said deed and by which his right has not been lost. In cross-examination the plaintiff stated that it is not a fact that the suit land has been declared as abandoned property by notification. The defendant No. 4 was not a party in OC, Suit No. 131 of 1982 and he does not know whether the Government preferred an appeal against the decree of the suit and it is stated that it is not a fact that the defendant is not aware of the said Title Suit No. 131 of 1982 and he did not file any application for cancellation of the sale deed dated 4-10-80 and he stated that he filed OC Suit No. 139 of 1982 and in that suit he stated that he went to perform Hajj on 25-11-71 and he further stated that he did not state that he went for performing Hajj in January, 1971. He denied that he did not come to Bangladesh on 10-9-76. He does not know about the possession being given to Sena Kallayan Sangstha on 14-12-72. He went to Settlement Office but he did not file any suit for mutation and he came to know about the possession of the Sena Kallayan Sangstha at the time of institution of OC Suit No. 139 of 1982. He further stated in cross-examination that it is not a fact that he did not manage the suit land from 16-12-71 and he also was not aware of value of the suit land which will be not more than 3 lacs. He knew that the property was sold to Sena Kallayan Sangstha on 4-10-80, it is not a fact that the defendants were in possession from 14-12-72 and and he was not cross-examined by the Government defendant No. 1

9. Abdul Wares, the sole witness, deposed on behalf of defendant Nos. 3 and 4, has stated that the suit land was declared abandoned on 14-12-72 by a notification Ext A. He states that the plaintiff has got licence and passbook which is marked as Ext B. That Ext. 0 is the sale deed in favour of the Sena Kallayan Sangstha executed on 4-10-80. Ext.D is the Mutation in favour of the defendant No. 4 and the plaintiff contested the said mutation proceeding and he lost there vide Exts E and E (1). He further stated that the original copy of judgment of the mutation proceeding was filed in OC Suit No. 139 of 1982. He also stated that the rent was paid to the Government by rent receipts vide Ext. F series. This defendant No. 4 also filed copy of the Gazette Notification Ext. J and he stated in the OC Suit No. 131 of 1982 they were not made parties and against the decree of the said suit Government preferred an appeal being Title Appeal No. 385 of 1988 which is still pending in the Lower Appellate Court and to that effect a certificate from the Advocate was filed vide Ext K. He further stated that the plaintiff has no possession in the suit land. The present value of the suit land will be Taka 38 lakh and it is not a fact that the plaintiff having kept his family members here left for Hajj in 1971 and he further stated that by the citizenship Certificate granted by Government, the plaintiff will not get the suit property back vide Ext L and he stated that it is not a fact that they were illegally possessing the Suit land or they were bound by the decree of OC Suit No. 131 of 1982. In cross-examination this witness stated that Sena Kallayan Sangstha is not a self earning agency and he does not know from which date the Sena Kallayan Sangstha came into being and he has no personal knowledge about the plaintiff''s sons, daughters and his residence but he could say by seeing the records. The witness stated that the sons and daughters of the plaintiff used to read in the Saint Joseph School from 1971 is not correct; that he had no idea as to where they resided before 14-12-72. He does not know about any writ case being filed by the plaintiff in the High Court Division. He further stated that it is not a fact that the suit land is a residential house. He does not know whether any Rule was issued in Writ Petition and he denied that during the pendency of the suit for possession the sale deed was executed and no payment was made and he stated that it was donated by the Government and there was no payment of consideration money; he does no know who filed OC Suit No. 131 of 1982 and they did not challenge the said decree but the Government has challenged. There were goods in the suit property when possession was taken and he further stated that he does not know as to how the property was taken over as an abandoned property. He stated that the plaintiff made a false statement and he does not know whether the sons and daughters of the plaintiff were here or not. It is not a fact that the Ext L has been prepared by him and value of the land will not be taka two lakh.

10. That the trial Court upon consideration of the aforesaid evidence found:

“সরকার বিবাদী পক্ষে দাখিী কোন দলিলে নালিশী সম্পত্তি পরিত্যাক্ত সম্পত্তি হিসাবে তালিকা ভুক্ত হইয়াছে এইরুপ কোন প্রকার দলিল পত্র নাই। সরকার পক্ষে নালিশী তফশীলের সম্পত্তি পরিত্যাক্ত বলিয়া দাবী করিলেও বিবাদীর দাখিলী প্রদর্শনী ’এ’ এবং প্রদর্শনী ‘জে’ দলিলে আদৌ নালিশী সম্পত্তির কোন উল্লেখ নাই। তদুপরি বাদীর দাখিলী প্রদর্শনী-৫ দলিলে সরকারের সংশ্লিষ্ট পরিত্যাক্ত কার্য্যালয় হইতে নালিশী সম্পত্তি আদৌ পরিত্যাক্ত সম্পত্তি হিসাবে তালিকাভুক্ত করা হয় নাই মর্মে গত ১৫-১২-৯১ ইং তারিখে বাদীকে লিখিত নির্বাহী প্রকৌশলী পরিত্যাক্ত হাউজেস, চট্টগ্রম অফিস হইতে জানাইয়াছে।”

and upon consideration of the evidence on record the learned trial Court also found that the plaintiff filed other suit No. 131 of 1982 and obtained a decree against the Government and the decree of that suit is still in force and it has been proved by Ext K. and it was further found by the learned trial Court that the said decree has not yet been set aside and the learned trial Court, relying upon the defendant Ext A and J and the plaintiff''s decree of the said suit of 1982, came to the finding to the effect that :

“বাদী নালিশী সম্পত্তিতে স্বত্ববান হওয়ার বিষয় প্রমান করিতে সক্ষম হইয়াছে। নালিশী সম্পত্তি সরকার কর্তৃক কখন ও আইন সংগতভাবে পরিত্যাক্ত সম্পত্তি হিসাবে কোন কোন গেজেট নোটিফিকেশন করা হয় নাই। বস্তুতঃ বিবাদীর দাখিলী দলিলপত্র আদৌ নালিশী সম্পত্তি পরিত্যাক্ত সম্পত্তি হিসাবে তালিকাভুক্ত দেখা যায় না। বরং বিবাদী অবিরোধীয়” কেস নং মেটাল ইন্ডাষ্ট্রিজ” নামে একটি শিল্প প্রতিষ্ঠান সরকার কর্তৃক পরিত্যাক্ত ঘোষনার বিষয়ে প্রদর্শনী ‘এ’ ও প্রদর্শনী ‘জে’ দলিলে দেখা যায়।”

and further the trial Court, having considered both oral and documentary evidence on record, found that the suit is not barred by limitation and decided the issues Nos. 1-5 in favour of the plaintiff.

11. It is necessary to mention here that during the pendency of this appeal, the plaintiff respondent filed an application for additional evidence to be admitted in this appeal and said application was heard by us and upon hearing we passed order that the said application would be considered at the time of hearing of the appeal. We have allowed the said application and the appeal has been taken up for hearing.

<u>12. Mr Md. Nurullah, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant submits that admittedly the plaintiff respondent obtained an ex parte decree earlier in Other Suit No. 131 of 1982 which was a suit for mere declaration and on the basis of which the respondent is not entitled to seek further relief in the subsequent suit ie the present suit for recovery of possession and, as such, suit is not maintainable. His further submission is that the plaintiff-respondent has stated in this suit that he left Dhaka for Hajj in January, 1971 whereas in Other Suit No. 139 of 1982 he made an averment that he left Dhaka for Hajj on 25th of November, 1971 and from this contradictory statement it is not certain as to when he left this country and the learned trial Court failed to consider the said contradictory statement of the plaintiff in assessing the evidence on record and erred in law in decreeing the suit; his next submission is that the learned trial Court misread and misconstrued the provision of President''s Order No. 149 of 1972. Bangladesh Citizenship (Temporary Provisions) Order 1972 as well as the provisions of Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1972 and President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 relating to abandonment of the property and the impugned decree is bad in law and cannot be sustained. It is further submitted that when any property is taken over under President''s Order 16 of 1972 it shall vest in the Government and such taking over or vesting of the property cannot be called in question by any court and in view of the provisions of Martial Law Regulation No. VII of 1977 the suit shall abate and shall not be further proceeded with and the trial Court ought to have dismissed the suit being not maintainable and the said Regulation is protected by paragraph 18 of the 4th Schedule of the Constitution.</u>

13. The learned Advocate for the appellant further submitted that the learned trial Court had no jurisdiction to try the suit and erred in law in framing the issue No. 3 and the findings and decisions arrived at are all erroneous and liable to be set aside.

14. Nurullah further submits that in view of the materials on record the learned Subordinate Judge failed to consider the Exts E, F, G, H series and Ext. 1 which do not establish the right, title, interest and possession of the plaintiff and, as such, the findings and decisions arrived at by the learned trial Court cannot be sustained in law and he further contends that the plaintiff is out of possession and the ex parte decree obtained by him in Other Suit No. 131 of 1982 having not been put into execution cannot be sustained and finding of the court below to the effect that the said ex parte decree is still in force is erroneous.

15. It has lastly been submitted by the appellant''s learned Advocate that the nationality certificate granted to the plaintiff cannot and should not be given retrospective effect as the plaintiff has already lost his right in the property and the property already vested in the Government and the Acting President''s Order 1 or 1972 and President''s Order 16 of 1672 have been protected by the 3rd paragraph of 4th Schedule of the Constitution of Bangladesh.

16. Mr M I Farooqui, the learned Advocate for the respondent, on the other hand, submits that the plaintiff never lost his citizenship and the suit property has not been declared as abandoned property by Exhibits A and J of the paper book and, as such, the trial Court is perfectly justified in decreeing the suit and the learned court below properly assessed the oral and documentary evidence on record. His next submission is that admittedly the plaintiff obtained an ex parte decree in the said Other Suit No. 131 of 1982 and that decree has been challenged by the Government by appeal which is pending and the decree stands until it is set aside. Mr. Farooqui lastly submits that neither the provision of MLR 7 of 1977, nor the provision of paragraph 18 of the 4th Schedule of the Constitution has any manner of application in facts and circumstances of the case and the plaintiff''s present suit is quite maintainable.

17. In this appeal large number of grounds have been taken but the moot question that calls for our consideration is whether the instant suit is maintainaible or not and it was also the whole argument of the learned Advocate of the appellant.

18. In elaborating the question of maintainability of the suit Mr Nurullah, the learned Advocate for the appellant, has argued that the suit property (the land and building) has been treated as abandoned property in view of the terms of paragraphs 4 and 5 of the said Martial Law Regulation No. VII of 1977, if any property is treated as abandoned property either under Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1972 or under President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 shall vest in the Government and such taking over or vesting of the property shall not be called in question by any court on any ground whatsoever and, as such, the instant suit is liable to be dismissed being not maintainable. The Regulation Nos. 4 and 5 of the Martial Law Regulation No.VII of 1977.

19. The Abandoned Properties (Supplementary Provisions) Regulation, 1977 reads as follows:

"4. Vesting of abandoned property, where, before the commencement of this Regulation, any property or the possession, control, management, administration or other rights of, or in respect of, any property, has been or is purported to have been taken over under the Acting President''s Order or as abandoned property in pursuance of the President''s Order by, or under the authority or at the instance of, the Government such property shall, notwithstanding any defect in the right or authority to take it over, vest, and be deemed always to have vested, in the Government,

5. Taking over, etc, of abandoned property not to be challenged, etc,

(1) Save as provided in the President''s Order, no such taking over or vesting of property as is referred in paragraph 4 shall be called in question on any ground whatsoever before any authority or in any Court, nor shall any such taking over or vesting of property give rise to any claim to compensation.

(2) All suits, appeals, petitions, applications and other legal proceedings pending immediately before the commencement of this Regulation in any Court in which any such taking over or vesting of property as is referred to in paragraph 4 has been called in question in any manner whatsoever shall abate forthwith and shall not be further proceeded with."

20. In support of his above contention Mr M Nurullah relied on the decisions reported in 30 DLR (SC) 207 in the case of Halima Khatun vs. Bangladesh and he also placed reliance on the case Nasir Uddin vs Govt. of Bangladesh reported in 32 DLR (AD) 216 and submitted that the plaintiff''s suit is not maintainable as it has abated. Let us consider the two decisions. In Halima Khatun''s case the two Writ petitions were dismissed by the High Court Division. In one Rice Mill at Khulna as abandoned property and in another Bangladesh Glass Works in Bogra as abandoned property were challenged. The Writ petition in one was dismissed earlier on the ground that the determination of the dispute whether the property was abandoned property was a disputed question of fact and could not be resolved by the affidavit of the parties, and, in the other, on the ground that the properties were rightly declared as abandoned property. In the context of the facts of those cases it was ordered that the Writ had abated in terms of regulation of MLR VII of 1977 by the High Court Division and on appeal before the Appellant Division affirmed the decision of the High Court and their Lordships of the Appellate Division held:

21. As to the contention of Mr MH Khondker that the Regulation did not aim at stifling any suit or petition or other legal proceedings which involved the question whether any property taken by the Government is abandoned property or not or that, if at all the Regulation appears to have intended to exclude the Court''s jurisdiction, it only intended to do so in respect of property which is actually abandoned property within the meaning of the Abandoned Property order a careful examination of the provisions would show otherwise. For the language in paragraph 4 of the Regulation has clearly laid down that any property which has been or is ''purported" to have been taken over as abandoned property under the Abandoned Property Order by or under the authority or at the instance of the government, such property shall notwithstanding any defect in the right or authority to take it over, vest in the Government. In paragraph 5 it is provided that such taking over or vesting of property shall not be called in question on any ground whatsoever before any authority or in any Court. Further, no person who may be affected by such taking over or vesting of property in the Government could claim any compensation. In consequence of these express provisions it would be merely knocking one''s head against a stone wall if one makes an attempt to get redress in a Court of law which, previous to this Regulation, might have granted relief if one could show that one''s property did not come within the purview of the Abandoned Property Order"

22. As regards the question whether the petitions before us have abated or not, or whether they can be further proceeded with we are of the view that the legislative directions as contained in sub-paragraph 2 of paragraph 5 of the impugned regulation are unequivocal and clear-Abatement in the context of Regulation connotes an idea of to demolish or to put an end to so that nothing survives. The answer to the question whether the petitions have abated or not cannot but be in the affirmative."

21. In Halima Khatun''s case the decision is that if any action of taking over or vesting of a property comes within the mischief of Martial Law Regulation VII of 1977 any proceeding seeking to challenge the taking over or vesting shall abate. In one case of Nasiruddin the fact is Md. Ahmed Husain got a lease for 99 years from the Govt. in 1963 of plot No. 10 A/4-4, Mirpur Housing Estate Dhaka with a house standing thereon and obtained possession in the same year. Appellant Nasiruddin on 13-10-71 entered into a contract to purchase the property with the owner lessee and in performance of the contract got possession of the premises. The contract was not completed by sale and after liberation the appellant brought Title Suit No. 95 of 1975 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka impleading the Government of Bangladesh which was decreed ex-parte on 5-12-77 and in execution case a sale deed was registered through Court. Earlier to that on 17-10-77 Martial Law Regulation No. VII of 1977 was promulgated the appellant filed writ petition No. 296 of 1978 challenging a notice being Memo dated 21-3-78 issued by Abandoned Property authority asking him to hand over possession of the property in default he will be liable to be evicted, the writ petition was taken up for hearing on 13-12-79 when the order set out above was made and so far the appellant is concerned. High Court Division has directed the abatement of a writ petition in view of sub-paragraph (1) of paragraph 5 read with paragraph 4 Martial Law Regulation No. VII of 1977. The appellant challenged the said order of abatement before the Appellate Division. Their Lordships excepting proposition of Halima Khatun''s case on the question statement, certain clarification was made and held:

"11. We do not feel that any further discussion is called for on the point, excepting making some clarification on the decision made in Halima Khatun''s case as stated earlier. In Halima Khatun''s case the decision is that if any action of taking over or vesting of a property comes within the mischief of Martial Law Regulation VII of 1977, any proceedings seeking to challenge the taking over or vesting of such property shall abate. The further observation that requires to be made is that abatement of the proceedings will follow in such cases, except where the taking over or vesting is without jurisdiction or coram non judice or it is mala fide and, in such circumstances, such action or order is not protected under the said Regulation with this clarification in Halima Khatun''s case and in conformity of the two decisions set out is to be held that there cannot be any question of abatement of any legal proceedings taken by an aggrieved person to protect his legal right or interest in the property against which action has been taken or vesting order made which is without jurisdiction or coram non judice or mala fide. Except within this narrow compass the proceedings coming within the mischief of MLR VII of 1977 shall abate."

22. Repelling the above contentions of Mr Nurullah, the learned Advocate for the respondent Mr Farooqul submits that there cannot be any dispute as to the principle and proposition of law laid down in those decisions but Mr Farooqui submits that the instant suit does not come under the mischief of the aforesaid provision of the said Martial Law Regulation and the question of protection under paragraph 18 of the 4th Schedule of the Constitution of Bangladesh does not also arise because of the fact that there is no mention about any residential property being treated as abandoned property in the Notification issued by the Government vide Ext J. and Ext A dated 31-12-72 and 14-12-72 respectively and, as such, it proves the assertion of the plaintiff that the suit property is not an abandoned property and the plaintiff has got a legal right to protect his interest in the property.

23. Secondly, M I Farooqui, submits that the plaintiff who came to Bangladesh in September, 1976 swore an affidavit of allegiance to Bangladesh surrendering his Pakistani passport and was granted citizenship certificate on 7-4-78 Ext B of the application for additional evidence and thereafter the plaintiff made a representation to the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong for consideration in the meeting of the Management Board of Abandoned Properties (Residential Houses) Chittagong Division and accordingly, the plaintiff was informed vide Ext 5 dated 15-12-81 to the effect that his residential house has neither been declared nor enlisted as abandoned under President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 and considering the submissions of the learned Advocates in the light of the aforesaid provisions of law and the decisions, we find substance in the contention of Mr Farooqui as the facts of the instant case and the facts as emerged from the aforesaid decisions are quite distinguishable and those decisions and the provisions of law cannot be applied in the instant case. Mr Farooqui has next submitted that the property of the absentee owners during the liberation period shall be declared as abandoned by the Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1972 and President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 under certain circumstance and in support of his contention he has referred to the case of Speed Navigation vs. Bangladesh reported in 27 DLR 175 where their Lordships of the High Court Division held:

"the properties of those absentee owners about whose purpose of staying outside the country the Government has not as yet formed any opinion whatsoever cannot also be regarded as abandoned properties, but the properties of those persons about whose purpose of staying abroad the Government has formed an adverse opinion, shall be deemed to be abandoned properties".

24. Citing the decision Mr Farooqui argues that there must be the Government''s opinion expressed as to the purpose of such person''s absence without which the property cannot be treated as abandoned property and Mr Farooqui also cited 31 DLR (SC) at 101 where-in their Lordships affirmed the decision of the case of 27 DLR and held: "In the instant case under appeal, the High Court Division has rightly found that the Government did not form any opinion as to whether the respondent in question and the assets thereof were abandoned properties that the Government is not competent to delegate that responsibility to any other authority for making such a decision or forming such an opinion, and that in the absence of any opinion that KP Mahmud was away from the country for any purpose prejudicial to the interest of Bangladesh, the respondent firm cannot be treated as an abandoned property and as such, the impugned order and the notification have rightly been found to have been passed without any lawful authority and, are as such, of no legal effect."

25. In view of the aforesaid decisions we hold that the plaintiff''s suit land and building is not an abandoned property from the'' legal point of view as well as from factual aspect of the case.

26. Mr Farooqui further submitted that to declare a property as abandoned by the Government it is for the Government to satisfy itself and to satisfy the Court as to the decision by formation of an opinion to the effect that the absence of the plaintiff is prejudicial to the interest of the State of Bangladesh and here it is significant that the Government has not appeared in this case and no such materials whatsoever were placed before this Court to the satisfaction of the Court and about any formation of opinion to show that the property is actually an abandoned one nor any Notification of the concerned Ministry of the Government has been filed by the appellant, rather from the Government paper vide Ex 5 Ext A and Ext J it appears that the suit property is not an abandoned property, as such, the question of application of the provisions of Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1971, the provision of President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 and the provision of MLR VII of 1977 does not arise and, as such, we find force in the argument of Mr Farooqui.

27. Mr Farooqui does not dispute that the action taken under the provision of MLR VII of 1977 and protection given by paragraph 18 of the 4th Schedule of the Constitution during the period of the Martial Law cannot be challenged and submits that it cannot also be said that protection will be a continuous process. The said constitutional provision does not say so and he submits that the protection under the said paragraph 18 of the Constitution is past and closed transaction. He also submits that in view of such a situation and the position of law, the Government has subsequently promulgated the Ordinance No. 54 of 1985 for the purpose of deciding the disputed questions arising out of the abandoned properties already declared by Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1972 and under President''s Order 16 of 1972 by establishing a Court of Settlement otherwise the Govt. could not have promulgated the said Ordinance. The paragraph 18 of the 4th Schedule of the Constitution reads as follows:

"18. All Proclamations, Proclamation Orders, Martial Law Regulations, Martial Law Orders and other laws made during the period between the 15th August, 1975, and the 9th April, 1979 (both days inclusive) all amendments, additions, modifications, substitutions and commissions made in this Constitution during the said period by such Proclamation, all others made, acts and things done, and actions and proceedings taken, or purported to have been made, done or taken, by any person or authority during the said period in exercise of the powers derived or purported to have been derived from any such Proclamation. Martial Law Regulation, Martial Law Order or any other law, or in execution of or in compliance with any order made or sentence passed by any court, tribunal or authority in the exercise or purported exercise of such powers. are hereby rectified and confirmed and are declared to have been validly made, done or taken and shall not be called in question before any Court, tribunal or authority on any ground whatsoever."

28. From the reading of the above paragraph of the 4th Schedule of the Constitution it appears that all actions taken during the Martial Law period were valid between the period 5th August, 1975 and 9th April, 1979 and confirmed and declared to have been made, done or taken and shall not be called in question in any Court, Tribunal or authority on any ground whatsoever. We find force in the contention of Mr Farooqui.

29. As we have already held that the Suit Property is not an abandoned property the question of the protection under the aforesaid constitutional provision does not arise in this case.

30. It is the case of the plaintiff that his industrial concern namely, Fasons Metal Industries Ltd. was declared as an abandoned property vide Ext. A and J under Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1972 and President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 but during the Martial Law period no action was taken regarding the transfer of the said industry to the appellant and it was after withdrawal of Martial Law, the Government transferred the said industry to the respondent No. 4 on 4-10-80 by the registered deed of sale Ext C and from the said Ext C the learned Advocate for the appellant tried to argue that in the schedule of the said Ext C included the suit property of the instant case but we find this is not correct as the plot No. of the suit property of the plaint are quite different from the scheduled of Ext C. Even if the Schedule of the suit property is included in Ext C we are afraid that by mere inclusion of the suit property in the schedule of Ext C can be treated as abandoned property in view of the settled principal of law.

<u>31. The learned trial Court having considered the Ext A, Ext J and Ext. 5 respectively rightly came to his finding and decision and we do not find any illegality in the impugned Judgment and decree as we have already held that the suit is maintainable and the plaintiff''s property with residential building was not declared as abandoned the present suit does not come either under the mischief of the MLR No. VII of 1977 or under the aforesaid provisions of the Constitution and the said President''s Order.</u>

32. Mr Nurullah, the learned Advocate for the appellant, has drawn our attention that in the plaint of the instant suit it has been stated by the plaintiff that he left Dhaka for Hajj in January, 1971 whereas he made a contradictory statement in other suit No. 139 of 1982 by stating that he left for Hajj in November, 1971 but the plaintiff in his cross-examination has stated, “আমি অপর ১৩৯/১৯৮২ নং মামলা করি। ঐ মামলায় বলে যে ২৫-১১-১৯৭১ সনে হজ্জ করিতে যাই। আমি বলি নাই যে, জানুয়ারী ৩/১৯৭১ সনে হজ্জে যাই।”

and his denial has not been disproved by the appellant rather from the written statement filed by the defendant appellant as well as other defendants we find that it was admitted that in the last part of 1971, when the defeat of the Pakistani Army was imminent the plaintiff left this country for Pakistan with the help of Pakistani Army. So the appellant could not prove that the plaintiff left Dhaka for performing Hajj in January, 1971 and the fact remains that he was away from the country during the last part of the period of liberation which has been admitted by the defendants in their written statements. It appears that the Government having been satisfied granted citizenship of Bangladesh to plaintiff vide Ext. B of the application of additional evidence which reads as follows:

No. 39-Citz./1-330/1976.

The Bangladesh Citizenship (TP) Order 1972

(Vide Article 4 of the Order) Form A-1.

Certificate of Citizenship

Whereas Sufi Fazle Ahmed has applied for a

certificate of citizenship, alleging with respect to himself the

particulars set out below, and has

satisfied the Government that the conditions laid down in Article 4 of the above mentioned order for the grant of a certificate of citizenship are fulfilled in the said Sufi Fazle Ahmed''s case.

Now therefore, in pursuance of the powers conferred by the said order and the Rules made thereunder, the Government hereby grant to the said Sufi Fazle Ahmed this certificate of citizenship of Bangladesh and declare that subject to the provision of the said order he shall be deemed to be a citizen of Bangladesh and shall be entitled to all the rights, privileges and capacities to which a citizen of Bangladesh is entitled to and shall also be subject to all the obligations, duties and liabilities of a citizen of Bangladesh under any or all the laws of Bangladesh. In witness wherefore I have here-to subscribed my name this 7th day of April, 1978  Signed (A M Chowdhury) For Secretary to the Govt. of the People''s Republic of Bangladesh.

33. From reading of the said certificate it appears that the plaintiff was conferred all rights and obligations as a citizen of Bangladesh. Further, it is the case of the plaintiff that he alone left Bangladesh keeping his wife and children here at Chittagong and thereafter one Mr S M Elias brought them to Dhaka at Mohammadpur and this statement of the plaintiff was not challenged by the appellant in cross examination and in the written statement the defendant Nos. 3 and 4 stated that the plaintiff left along with Pakistani Army but that statement was also not proved by the defendants by any other evidence. So we find that the plaintiff alone left the country in the last part of 1971 as admitted by the appellant in their written statement and the learned trial Court rightly considering both oral and documentary evidence on record correctly found that the property has not been included in Ext J and A of the paper book as noticed earlier and discussed.

34. Mr Nurullah, the learned Advocate also argued that the nationality certificate could not be given retrospective effect. Mr Farooqui, on the other hand, submits that the Government having been satisfied issued citizenship certificate with all rights and obligations and we hold that once citizenship, certificate is granted it is granted for all practical purpose we find substance in the submission of Mr Farooqui in this regard.

35. For the reasons stated above we do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment and decree passed by the trial Court.

36. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs. The connected Rule being Civil Rule No. 177 (F) of 1990 is discharged.

A M Mahmudur Rahman J : I have heard the judgment delivered by my learned brother and I agree with the conclusion. But I am inclined to express my view on certain points mooted at the Bar.

38. As the facts of the instant case has elaborately been stated by my learned brother in his judgment I need not report the same.

39. The appellant contended that the suit for eviction on the basis of the ex parte decree made in OC Suit No. 131 of 1982 is not maintainable as the property was treated as abandoned property under Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1972 and President''s Order No. 16 of 1971 and such action in treating the property was protected under Regulation No. 5 of the Regulation No. VII of 1977 which debars a person from questioning the authority for an action taken or purported to have been taken under Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1972 or President''s Order No. 16 of 1972.

<u>40. My reading of both the laws is that those provisions are applicable to a suit or a proceeding either before a Court or Tribunal before which the order or act or action taken or done either under Acting President''s Order 1 of 1972 or President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 is challenged. On reference to the relief sought for in the suit those provisions do not apply as the relief sought in the present suit was for recovery of possession on eviction of the defendants. It was further contended that in view of the conflicting statements as to leaving of the respondent from former East Pakistan the suit fails. The plaintiff averred in the plaint that he left former East Pakistan in January, 1971 to perform Hajj but in the statement before the Court in OC Suit No. 139 of 1982 he stated that he left Bangladesh on November 25, 1971 for Mecca. It is found from the judgment of the Other Appeal No. 139 of 1982, Ext. A, the Court of appeal below states, “১৯৭১ ইংরাজীতে বাদী পবিত্র হজ্জ পালন সহ বিভিন্ন তীর্থস্থান পরিদর্শনের উদ্দেশ্যে তৎকালীন পূর্ব পাকিস্থানের বাহিরে অবস্থান করে। ঐ সময় বাদী পাকিস্থানী পাসপোর্ট গ্রহন করে। গত ২৫-১১-৭১ ইং তারিখে হজ্জ পালনের উদ্দেশ্যে মক্কা শরীফে যান”।</u>

41. Mr Nurullah also vigorously canvassed before us that the conflicting statement on leaving of the respondent from former East Pakistan cannot be taken as evidence to hold that the respondent left Bangladesh on 25-11-1971 as acceptance of such evidence out of a pleading cannot be foundation of the finding of a court. I have perused the statement in the plaint wherein it is stated that the plaintiff left Bangladesh in January, 1971, Mr Nurullah in elaborating the submission says that unless the plaint is amended to the effect that the plaintiff left on November 25, 1971 the statement which he made in the Other Suit No. 139 of 1982 cannot be relied upon for holding that the plaintiff left in November, 1971. He further argued that the weakness of the defence is no foundation for success of the plaintiff. Rather it is for the plaintiff to succeed on his own case. This proposition of law does not admit of any doubt. It is also correct that without amending the plaint no evidence can be led to prove a case of the plaintiff which has not been made out in the plaint. The decision in the case of Lala Hakim Rai vs. Lala Ganga Ram 1942 PC 62 relied upon by Mr Nurullah, Messrs Trojan and Co. vs. Nagappa Chettiar. 1953 (SC) 253 support the view.

<u>42. The contention on formation of opinion as to whether the property is abandoned one within the meaning of section 2 (1) (ii) (a) President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 is applicable to a case where the propriety of abandonment is questioned which is absent in the present case. Mr Farooqui argued that Regulation 4 of Martial Law Regulation No. 7 of 1977 is not protected under Paragraph 18 of the Constitution. According to him, Paragraph 18 protects the instrument described thereunder made during the period between 15th August, 1975 and 9th April 1979 (both days inclusive). My reading of Paragraph No. 18 is that it has no application to the fact of the present case insomuch as it speaks of orders made, acts and things done, and actions and proceedings taken, or purported to have been made, done or taken by any person or authority during the said period in exercise of the power derived or purported to have been derived from such proclamation, Martial Law Regulation, Martial Law Order or any other law, or in execution of or in compliance with any order made or sentence passed by any Court, tribunal or authority in the exercise or purported exercise of such powers, are hereby ratified and confirmed and are declared to have been validly made, done or taken and shall not be called in question in or before any court, tribunal or authority on any ground whatsoever. Paragraph 18 speaks for the purpose during the said period. The action in placing the property under the authority is sought to be recovered in the present suit was taken on 22-12-1971 from the son of the respondent Najar Mainuddin by the Government. Thus I hold paragraph 18 is irrelevant for our purpose. The question regarding the nature of the property has to be dealt with under President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 and Martial Law Regulation No. 7 of 1977. That has to be done in the suit which was instituted for seeking relief to the effect that the property therein is an abandoned property. It was further argued by Mr Farooqui that the suit is maintainable in view of the provision of Ordinance 54 of 1985 inasmuch as it speaks that the suit for declaration that an action taken under President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 on promulgation of the aforesaid Ordinance shall be dealt with by the Court of Settlement constituted under that Ordinance. This contention again goes back to the root of challenging the order or action or purported action in placing the property in suit under any authority or body or person by the Government or the action taken or purported to have been taken either under Acting President''s Order No. 1 of 1972 or President''s Order No. 16 of 1972 at the instance of the Government. This requires to be examined in a suit where such action is challenged. But not here. We are concerned only whether, on the findings of the court below, the present decree can be sustained. I find that the trial Court found on evidence that the defendant failed to produce any document indicating that the Government formed opinion and the property in suit were taken over by the Government on the basis of the evidence produced before it. The question of validity or otherwise of the action in taking over the property by the Government and subsequent transfer of the property is a matter for the appellate Court to discuss. If the appellant succeeds in the appeal from the decree passed in OC suit No. 139 of 1982 the appellant will be entitled to restitution of the property under section 144 of the CPC. In view of the facts of the present case we are not called upon to decide whether the property satisfies the character of an abandoned property or whether the action in taking over the property followed by subsequent transfer to the defendant No. 4 is valid in law or not as conclusion on this point will be prejudging the whole matter pending in the court below. The contention on losing citizenship of the appellant again rests on the averment whether he left in January or in November, 1971 This has to be seen in the appeal from the decree of OC Suit No. 139 of 1982. Although very illuminating address was made on domicile, citizenship, accrual of citizenship and grant of citizenship I do not think that in this present suit there is any scope for making elaborate discussion on this point in this regard on the plea of restrospectivity of the grant of citizenship.</u>

43. Mr Nurullah further argued with reference to the eviidence adduced in the OC Suit No. 139/82 that merely saying that documents marked Ext. 1-5 for the plaintiff in the case is proved is not enough. It was the requirement of law even in making the ex parte decree by the trial Court speak as to the nature of the document and its legal consequence upon the decree to be made. We agree with Mr Nurullah. But in this case I do not think that the contention requires any adjudication at this stage.

In the result, I dismiss the appeal. No costs.

End.
